introduction_markdown:
Answer both questions beginning each answer on a new page in the answer booklet. Both answers carry equal marks.

Credit will be given for accuracy, correct use of a variety of expressions, verbs, vocabulary and idioms.

Use blue ink only.

You are reminded of the necessity for orderly presentation of your answers.
enonce_intro_markdown:
*Using a tense suitable to your chosen topic, write an essay in French, of at least 140 and not more than 150 words, (not counting figures, words in brackets, abbreviations and names of people or places) on ONE of the following topics.*

*Credit will be given for the correct use of a variety of expressions, verbs, vocabulary and idioms.*

*If you choose topic (b)your name must be Makumba and your address CES de Monkwo.*

*If you choose topic (c), your essay must be based on the events in the picture.*

*Off-topic material will earn no marks.*

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) La semaine nationale du bilinguisme vient de se terminer dans votre établissement. Ecrivez une lettre à votre camarade de classe qui n'a pas pu assister pour lui raconter cet évènement.

- Expliquez-lui les préparatifs,
- le déroulement des activités,
- et donnez-lui vos impressions personnelles.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Tense chosen:** the passé composé for what happened during the week, with the imparfait where a state or a feeling is described. The text is a letter to a classmate, so it has a place and date, an informal salutation (*Cher Paul*), a body, a closing formula and the signature *Makumba*; the address *CES de Monkwo* is the one required by the topic, and *tu* is used because the reader is a friend.

**Model essay** (149 words counted with the heading and signature; 143 without the names of people and places and the figure)

CES de Monkwo, le vendredi 12 mars

Cher Paul,

Tu n'as pas pu assister à la semaine nationale du bilinguisme, alors je t'écris pour tout te raconter. Pendant les jours précédents, nous avons préparé la fête avec nos professeurs : nous avons décoré la cour et répété des chansons et des sketchs en français et en anglais.

La semaine a commencé lundi par un défilé très coloré. Ensuite, il y a eu des concours de poésie, un débat et un grand spectacle de danse. Le directeur a remis des prix aux meilleures classes, et la nôtre a gagné le concours de théâtre. Le dernier jour, il a prononcé un discours sur l'importance d'apprendre deux langues.

Personnellement, j'ai beaucoup aimé cet événement, car j'ai amélioré mon anglais en parlant avec mes camarades. J'étais très fier de mon pays bilingue et de notre école. Tu nous as beaucoup manqué !

Ton ami,

Makumba

**Notes**

The letter follows the three parts of the topic: the preparations (decorating the yard, rehearsing songs and sketches in French and English), the course of the activities (parade, poetry contests, a debate, a dance show, prizes, the head teacher's speech) and the writer's personal impressions (enjoyed it, improved his English). The name Makumba and the address CES de Monkwo are imposed by the topic; the friend's first name (Paul) and the date are invented, and names of people and places are not counted in the word limit.

**Marking criteria**

| Criterion | What earns the marks |
|---|---|
| Accuracy | Correct verb forms, agreements, spelling and accents; correct use of the tense chosen |
| Variety of expressions | Linking words (*d'abord*, *puis*, *finalement*, *heureusement*) and set phrases |
| Variety of verbs | Several different verbs instead of *être*, *avoir* and *faire* only |
| Vocabulary and idioms | Words and expressions suited to the topic; idioms used correctly |
| Relevance and length | All three bullet points covered; between 140 and 150 words |

**Common mistakes**

1. Forgetting the letter format (address, date, salutation, closing) or not using the imposed name and address.
2. Using the wrong register: the letter goes to a classmate, so *tu* and an informal closing (*Ton ami*) are expected, not *vous* and *Veuillez agréer ...*.
